description: Reference set for Trojan Horse. Each entry maps one durable story to the four stages and six processes. See corpus.schema.json for the field rules.

stories.sum: A man who is good at everything takes ten years to learn the one thing that gets him home.
stories.s1: Seven years on Calypso's island, offered immortality. The comfort is real, and it is still the thing keeping him from home.
stories.s2: Every prop goes: fleet, crew, name, clothes. He washes up on Phaeacia with nothing, and has to ask for help.
stories.s3: Trapped in the cave by his own announcement, then held a full year by Circe without anyone raising the subject of leaving.
stories.s4: He builds the raft himself, waits in rags in his own hall, and strings the bow no one else can bend.
stories.pA: He stays seven years somewhere pleasant
stories.pB: He loses the fleet, the crew and his name
stories.pC: The crew opens the bag of winds in sight of Ithaca
stories.pD: He is shut in the cave by his own boast
stories.pE: A year passes on Circe's island before anyone mentions home
stories.pF: He builds the raft and strings the bow himself

stories.sum: A man withdraws over an insult, and the person who pays is the one who borrowed his armour.
stories.s1: Nine years of siege have become a routine with its own comforts. Everyone behaves as if the war is the permanent condition.
stories.s2: The quarrel strips the prize, the standing and then the friend. What is left is a man with nothing to defend but the grievance.
stories.s3: He sits by the ships repeating the same case to anyone sent to him. The tent is a cage he built and locked.
stories.s4: He returns to the field, and later hands the body back. The second act costs him more than the first.
stories.pA: The siege becomes a way of life
stories.pB: The prize and the standing are taken in public
stories.pC: Patroclus goes out in borrowed armour and does not come back
stories.pD: He argues the same grievance from inside the tent
stories.pE: Weeks pass with the ships beached and nothing moving
stories.pF: He gives the body back, which no rule required

stories.sum: A man keeps one small unglamorous act going for nineteen years and it turns out to be the whole plan.
stories.s1: Brooks cannot live outside the wall. The institution has become the map, and everyone inside calls that being settled.
stories.s2: The sentence takes the profession, the marriage, the name and the daylight. What arrives at the gate is a man with nothing.
stories.s3: The library, the tax returns, the routine. A comfortable position inside the cage that could have lasted the rest of his life.
stories.s4: A rock hammer and a poster. Nineteen years of the same small action, done nightly, with no way to check the progress.
stories.pA: Institutional routine becomes the only map anyone has
stories.pB: The trial takes his profession, his marriage and his name
stories.pC: He hands the warden a laundered fortune and gets years added
stories.pD: Solitary, and the loop of a conviction he cannot appeal
stories.pE: He builds a comfortable position inside the walls
stories.pF: A rock hammer, used nightly, for nineteen years

stories.sum: A man builds a whole life as an instrument for repeating one evening, and the instrument works perfectly.
stories.s1: The parties run weekly and go nowhere. The wealth is real; the map it was bought to reach was drawn in 1917.
stories.s2: Daisy in the room is smaller than the idea of her. The collision is not a disaster, it is an ordinary afternoon.
stories.s3: He cannot revise the plan. Every conversation is steered back to the same year, and the persona he built cannot say so.
stories.s4: There is no fourth stage. The story is what the pattern does when the ownership never arrives.
stories.pA: West Egg parties that repeat and reach nothing
stories.pB: The war and the missing years strip the original name
stories.pC: He lets Daisy drive, and takes the consequence
stories.pD: Every route leads back to one afternoon in 1917
stories.pE: Five years of arrangements that keep the plan comfortable
stories.pF: Absent — the performance stands where the tool should be

stories.sum: A man who needs certainty before acting builds a four-act delay and calls it caution.
stories.s1: Court life at Elsinore resumes quickly after the funeral. Everyone has agreed on a version of events, and it holds until it does not.
stories.s2: Father dead, mother remarried, throne taken. The certainties are gone in a single month and nothing has replaced them.
stories.s3: The performance of madness starts as cover and becomes the residence. He talks himself out of the act, in public, repeatedly.
stories.s4: It arrives in the final scene, unplanned, and works. Ownership taken that late is indistinguishable from accident.
stories.pA: The court settles back into its routine after the funeral
stories.pB: Father, mother, throne and certainty gone in a month
stories.pC: He stabs through a curtain without checking who is behind it
stories.pD: He argues the case against himself, out loud, repeatedly
stories.pE: The play, the pacing, the postponement — motion instead of movement
stories.pF: He acts in the last scene, unrehearsed

stories.sum: A man is shown the ordinary consequences of his own routine and changes it the same morning.
stories.s1: The counting house runs identically every day and every day is defensible. Thrift has been promoted from habit to principle.
stories.s2: Three nights strip the story he tells about himself: the childhood, the engagement he let lapse, the grave with his own name.
stories.s3: The miser was built in a cold room by a boy with no other options. It kept working long after the room was gone.
stories.s4: The turkey, the raise, the visit. All of it executed before noon, in public, at his own expense.
stories.pA: A daily routine so tight it cannot be questioned
stories.pB: Three nights remove every version he tells about himself
stories.pC: He let the engagement lapse and never revisited it
stories.pD: The same ledger, the same answer, for decades
stories.pE: Comfort by subtraction — nothing risked, nothing spent
stories.pF: The turkey, the raise and the visit, all before noon

stories.sum: Someone with no aptitude for it carries the thing the whole distance, and fails at the last step anyway.
stories.s1: The Shire is comfortable enough that it cannot picture the war. The map ends at the borders and nobody minds.
stories.s2: Home, company, health and the use of one hand, given up in stages. By Mordor there is nothing left to strip.
stories.s3: The ring's own loop: carrying it makes it heavier, and the weight is the argument for keeping it.
stories.s4: He walks the whole distance and fails at the crack. The ownership is the walking, which nobody else volunteered for.
stories.pA: A comfortable county that has not noticed the war
stories.pB: Home, health and company given up in stages
stories.pC: Boromir reaches for it, and the company breaks
stories.pD: The ring gets heavier the longer it is carried
stories.pE: Rivendell and Lothlórien, where time stops being counted
stories.pF: He walks the distance no one else volunteered for

stories.sum: A survival habit built for a poor district turns out to be exactly the wrong instinct inside a televised game.
stories.s1: District 12 is narrow enough to look like order. Keep your head down, work the fence, and the arrangement holds.
stories.s2: The reaping removes home, name and the option of not being watched. Every prop is replaced with a costume.
stories.s3: The girl on fire is built by stylists, then required of her. She cannot tell which of her reactions are hers.
stories.s4: The berries. She takes the game's own rule and hands it back, which is the one move the rule cannot absorb.
stories.pA: A district narrow enough to be mistaken for order
stories.pB: The reaping takes home, name and privacy at once
stories.pC: She trusts the arena's rules and they are changed mid-game
stories.pD: The tracker jacker loop, and the replays that follow
stories.pE: The victory tour: comfort offered as a permanent condition
stories.pF: The berries, offered on the game's own terms

stories.sum: A young man is waiting for his life to start and only moves once there is nothing left to wait for.
stories.s1: One more season on the farm. The plan is always next year, and the horizon is a chore list.
stories.s2: The farm burns with the family in it. There is no version of the old life to return to.
stories.s3: The farm boy who is not ready, repeated to himself and to anyone senior enough to contradict it.
stories.s4: He switches off the targeting computer and trusts the practice instead of the instrument.
stories.pA: One more season on the farm, every season
stories.pB: The farm burns and the family with it
stories.pC: He leaves training early and arrives unprepared
stories.pD: The loop of not being ready, said out loud
stories.pE: Waiting for a life to start somewhere else
stories.pF: He switches off the computer and trusts the training

stories.sum: A man discovers the comfortable version was manufactured, and that knowing it is not the same as being free.
stories.s1: The simulation is the first stage stated literally: a pleasant map, running on rails, mistaken for the terrain.
stories.s2: Unplugging takes the body, the job, the name and the daylight. What is left is worse than the lie and it is real.
stories.s3: He cannot believe he is the one. The doubt is not modesty, it is the loop that keeps him losing.
stories.s4: He stops dodging and stands still. The training was finished long before he was willing to use it.
stories.pA: A pleasant simulation running quietly on rails
stories.pB: Unplugging costs the body, the job and the name
stories.pC: He goes back in for Morpheus against every rule
stories.pD: The loop of not believing he is the one
stories.pE: The comfortable answer: take the blue pill and forget
stories.pF: He stops dodging and stands still

stories.sum: A boy accepts a story about his own guilt and spends years in a pleasant place to avoid checking it.
stories.s1: Everything the light touches. A certainty inherited whole, with no idea what it costs to hold.
stories.s2: The stampede takes the father, the home and the account of himself. He leaves with nothing but a version of events.
stories.s3: Hakuna matata is the third and fourth process in one phrase: a loop of guilt, wrapped in a routine that numbs it.
stories.s4: He walks back across the desert and says the true version out loud, in front of everyone who believed the other one.
stories.pA: A kingdom described as a certainty, never as a job
stories.pB: The stampede takes father, home and his account of himself
stories.pC: He goes to the gorge because his uncle suggested it
stories.pD: The same replayed guilt, unexamined for years
stories.pE: Hakuna matata: a routine built to keep the question away
stories.pF: He crosses the desert and states what happened

stories.sum: A father's vigilance is a reasonable response to a real catastrophe, and it is also the thing costing him his son.
stories.s1: The anemone, the schedule, the rules. Safety maintained by never going out, which everyone involved calls being careful.
stories.s2: The boat takes the boy. Every routine that was supposed to prevent this is still in place and none of it worked.
stories.s3: The loop is the promise: nothing will ever happen to you. It is unkeepable, and repeating it is the cage.
stories.s4: He lets go — of the reef, of the plan, and finally of the fin. Ownership here looks like doing less.
stories.pA: A reef-sized routine described as being careful
stories.pB: The boat takes the boy and no routine prevented it
stories.pC: He swims off in the wrong direction, twice, out of panic
stories.pD: The promise that nothing will ever happen, repeated
stories.pE: The safe schedule that keeps everyone home
stories.pF: He lets go of the fin and lets the boy swim

stories.sum: A man tries every way out of a repeating day and is only released by getting good at the day itself.
stories.s1: Contempt as a comfortable position. He has an answer for everything and it is the reason nothing changes.
stories.s2: The loop removes consequence, and with it every prop he used: the job, the future, the possibility of a next day.
stories.s3: He plays every angle, then stops trying. The stalled version lasts longer on screen than the escape attempts.
stories.s4: Piano, ice, medicine, one day at a time, with no way to bank the progress. This is the fourth stage as daily practice.
stories.pA: A repeating day with no consequence attached
stories.pB: The loop removes the job, the future and tomorrow
stories.pC: He games the day for advantage and loses more time
stories.pD: He runs the same day looking for an exit
stories.pE: He settles into the loop and stops trying to leave
stories.pF: Piano, ice and medicine, one unbankable day at a time

stories.sum: A woman refuses two comfortable arrangements that would have cost the same thing, and takes destitution instead.
stories.s1: Thornfield is warm, paid and pleasant. The map it draws requires one fact to stay in the attic.
stories.s2: She walks out with nothing, sleeps outdoors and nearly dies of it. The props are not stripped, she puts them down.
stories.s3: The self-sufficiency built in a cold childhood keeps working long past its use, and it nearly hands her to St John.
stories.s4: She goes back on her own terms, with her own money, and asks the question herself.
stories.pA: A warm, paid position with one fact kept upstairs
stories.pB: She walks out with nothing and sleeps in the open
stories.pC: She almost takes St John's offer out of exhaustion
stories.pD: The loop of being nobody's, argued in her own voice
stories.pE: Comfort at Thornfield, on terms she cannot examine
stories.pF: She returns with her own money and asks herself

stories.sum: A man with real skill points it at the wrong door and calls the whole thing provision for his family.
stories.s1: The classroom and the car wash. A life he never chose out loud, defended daily as the responsible option.
stories.s2: The diagnosis removes the timeline. Everything he was deferring is now on a clock he did not set.
stories.s3: Heisenberg is built to survive the box and then preferred to the man. By the end he says so plainly.
stories.s4: Absolute ownership, executed with genuine mastery, aimed away from home. The fourth stage does not guarantee the direction.
stories.pA: A life never chosen out loud, defended as responsible
stories.pB: The diagnosis takes the timeline he was counting on
stories.pC: Every impatient shortcut widens the damage
stories.pD: The loop of what he is owed, rehearsed for five seasons
stories.pE: The comfortable lab, the routine, the untouched money
stories.pF: Real mastery, taken up and pointed away from home

stories.sum: A sharp reader of people discovers her sharpest reading was wrong, and has to revise it in public.
stories.s1: Longbourn runs on a settled reading of everyone in it. First impressions have been promoted to knowledge.
stories.s2: Lydia's elopement removes the family's standing overnight. Every arrangement they were counting on stops being available.
stories.s3: The wit that protects her also keeps her from being read, and it makes the wrong judgement very hard to withdraw.
stories.s4: She revises the judgement, says so, and refuses Lady Catherine to her face. The reversal costs more than either refusal.
stories.pA: A settled reading of everyone, treated as fact
stories.pB: Lydia's elopement takes the family's standing overnight
stories.pC: She believes Wickham because he flatters her judgement
stories.pD: The first impression, defended long past its evidence
stories.pE: Longbourn's routine, where nothing has to be decided
stories.pF: She revises the judgement out loud and refuses Lady Catherine

stories.sum: A private injury is converted into everyone's course, and the ship is very well run all the way down.
stories.s1: The voyage has a stated commercial purpose. Every man aboard believes he signed on for oil.
stories.s2: The leg was taken before page one. The collision is old, and the whole book happens after it.
stories.s3: The pursuit is the cage. He is stuck in one loop and has the authority to make it everyone's route.
stories.s4: The harpoon is genuinely mastered. Ownership without a revised script is just a well-executed course into the water.
stories.pA: A commercial voyage everyone believes they signed for
stories.pB: The leg was taken before the book begins
stories.pC: He nails the doubloon to the mast and overrides every warning
stories.pD: One loop, held with the authority to enforce it
stories.pE: The routine of the hunt, which postpones the reckoning
stories.pF: Real mastery of the harpoon, aimed at one target

stories.sum: A child's map of a small town is corrected by watching an adult lose a case he was always going to lose.
stories.s1: Maycomb is a settled place with settled people, and the children have a complete map of it by page ten.
stories.s2: The verdict removes the assumption that the town is fair. Nothing about the town changes; the map does.
stories.s3: Boo Radley is the loop: a story repeated until nobody checks it, held in place by everyone's comfort.
stories.s4: Atticus takes the case knowing the outcome. The ownership is in the taking, not the winning.
stories.pA: A settled town with a complete and wrong map
stories.pB: The verdict removes the assumption of fairness
stories.pC: The children's raid on the Radley place nearly costs them
stories.pD: The Radley story, repeated until nobody checks it
stories.pE: Maycomb's routine, which is the whole defence of it
stories.pF: He takes the case knowing how it ends

stories.sum: A man keeps a private self as his whole strategy, and the state turns out to have planned for that.
stories.s1: The Ministry routine is survivable and that is exactly the problem. Nothing about the day requires him to notice it.
stories.s2: The arrest takes the room, the woman, the diary and the body. The strip is total and deliberate.
stories.s3: Room 101 is the cage stated plainly. The loop is not his to run any more; it is administered.
stories.s4: Refused. The book exists to show the pattern failing at the fourth stage, which is why it still gets read.
stories.pA: A survivable routine that never has to be examined
stories.pB: The arrest takes the room, the diary and the body
stories.pC: He trusts O'Brien on the strength of a look
stories.pD: Room 101, where the loop is administered to him
stories.pE: The room above the shop, where time is allowed to pass
stories.pF: Absent — the fourth stage is refused

stories.sum: A boy handed a destiny keeps discovering that the adults' plan for him is not the same as a plan.
stories.s1: The cupboard, then Hogwarts. Both are complete worlds with rules that arrive pre-decided.
stories.s2: Parents, godfather, mentor, certainty. The strip runs across seven books and takes something in each.
stories.s3: The loop is the prophecy: he keeps checking whether he was chosen or whether he chose, and cannot settle it.
stories.s4: He walks into the forest without a plan or a weapon, having decided what it is for.
stories.pA: Two complete worlds, both with pre-decided rules
stories.pB: Parents, godfather and mentor removed in turn
stories.pC: He goes to the Ministry on a vision he did not verify
stories.pD: The prophecy loop: chosen, or choosing
stories.pE: Terms at school where the war is somebody else's
stories.pF: He walks into the forest with no weapon

stories.sum: A woman decides to live before the ship hits anything, and the disaster only tests the decision.
stories.s1: First class is a cage with excellent food, and everyone in it agrees to describe the arrangement as good fortune.
stories.s2: The ship takes the fiancé, the fortune, the name and the plan. She arrives in New York with none of it.
stories.s3: The well-behaved daughter is the mask, and the engagement is the routine that keeps it in place.
stories.s4: The whistle. She blows it because she has already decided to live, and gives a stranger's name on the list.
stories.pA: First class, described by everyone as good fortune
stories.pB: Fiancé, fortune, name and plan gone in a night
stories.pC: The ship keeps its speed to make the schedule
stories.pD: The loop of what a daughter is required to be
stories.pE: An engagement that keeps everything comfortably fixed
stories.pF: She blows the whistle and gives a new name

stories.sum: A man has arranged his life so that nothing can be asked of him, and then something is.
stories.s1: The café runs itself. Neutrality has been promoted from a mood to a business model to a personality.
stories.s2: Ilsa walking in removes the arrangement. The version of the past he had settled on is no longer the version.
stories.s3: He sticks his neck out for nobody, said often enough that it counts as a loop rather than a policy.
stories.s4: He gives away the letters. It costs him the thing he wanted and he does it at the airport, in person.
stories.pA: A café and a neutrality that has become a personality
stories.pB: Ilsa arrives and the settled version of the past goes
stories.pC: He drinks through the night rather than ask her anything
stories.pD: He sticks his neck out for nobody, repeatedly
stories.pE: Casablanca itself: everyone waiting, nobody leaving
stories.pF: He hands over the letters at the airport

stories.sum: A man who has explained he is not part of the family takes it over completely, and never re-opens the question.
stories.s1: That's my family, it's not me. The sentence is the map, and it holds right up until it is needed.
stories.s2: The shooting of his father removes the separation. There is no version of the outside life still available.
stories.s3: The war hero who was never going to be in it. The mask is dropped, and what is under it is decisive.
stories.s4: Total ownership, executed with precision, in the wrong direction. The fourth stage says nothing about where you point it.
stories.pA: A sentence about not being part of it, used as a map
stories.pB: The shooting removes the separation entirely
stories.pC: Sonny drives out angry and is killed at the toll booth
stories.pD: The loop of one more thing before it is finished
stories.pE: Sicily, where the war is somewhere else
stories.pF: He takes it over completely, and closes the question

stories.sum: A man outsources his agency to a persona he invented, and has to take it back the hard way.
stories.s1: The catalogue apartment. Identity assembled by mail order, with insomnia as the only sign anything is wrong.
stories.s2: The explosion removes every object he had used to describe himself. The strip is literal and it is a relief.
stories.s3: Tyler starts as an escape from the box and ends up running the house. The cage is self-issued.
stories.s4: He shoots himself to retake authorship. Ownership arrives at the last possible price.
stories.pA: An identity assembled from a catalogue
stories.pB: The explosion removes every object he was using
stories.pC: Project Mayhem escalates past anything he intended
stories.pD: He argues with a persona he built himself
stories.pE: The support groups, which work and change nothing
stories.pF: He shoots himself to take the script back

stories.sum: A student mistakes an authority's approval for the goal, and only plays when he stops needing it.
stories.s1: Practice is the bubble. Every other part of a life is cut away and the cutting is described as seriousness.
stories.s2: The crash, the expulsion, the hearing. Career, teacher and the account of himself all go in one week.
stories.s3: The loop is whether he is one of the greats, run nightly, refereed by a man who benefits from the question.
stories.s4: He counts in the band and plays without permission. The mastery was already there; the ownership was not.
stories.pA: Practice used to cut away every other part of a life
stories.pB: The crash and the expulsion in one week
stories.pC: He drives to the gig injured rather than miss it
stories.pD: The nightly question of whether he is great
stories.pE: The safer band, where nobody is shouting
stories.pF: He counts in the band and plays without permission

stories.sum: An island rule that once kept everyone alive is now the reason the island is dying.
stories.s1: The reef is the edge of the map and nobody asks why. The rule was sound once and has outlived the reason.
stories.s2: The blight, the failing nets, her grandmother's death. The certainties are removed in order.
stories.s3: The dutiful daughter of the chief. The loop is her own question about whether the calling is allowed.
stories.s4: She learns wayfinding — an actual craft, on the water, badly at first — and returns the heart herself.
stories.pA: A rule at the reef that outlived its reason
stories.pB: The blight and the failing nets take the certainties
stories.pC: She sails out untrained and loses the boat
stories.pD: The loop of whether she is allowed to go
stories.pE: Village routine, which keeps the question comfortable
stories.pF: She learns wayfinding and returns the heart

stories.sum: A house kept exactly as it was is a promise being kept in the least useful possible way.
stories.s1: The house is preserved to the inch while the city is built over it. Preservation has become the whole plan.
stories.s2: Ellie's death, then the court order. The arrangement he was defending is removed by other people.
stories.s3: The grief is the furniture. The loop is a promise he has been keeping in the shape of an address.
stories.s4: He empties the house, object by object, to make it fly. The ownership is in the throwing out.
stories.pA: A house preserved to the inch as the entire plan
stories.pB: Ellie's death and the court order remove the arrangement
stories.pC: He hits the workman and loses the house in a morning
stories.pD: A promise kept in the shape of an address
stories.pE: Years of the same route, the same chair, the same day
stories.pF: He empties the house to make it fly

stories.sum: A child is put to work in a place that takes names, and the work is what gets her out.
stories.s1: A sulking child in the back of a car, certain the world is arranged around her preferences.
stories.s2: Parents turned to pigs, the way home gone, her own name taken by contract. Nothing familiar is left.
stories.s3: The bathhouse is a comfortable holding pattern that eats names. Everyone in it has stopped counting the years.
stories.s4: She works, remembers her own name, and walks out without looking back because she was told not to.
stories.pA: A child certain the world is arranged for her
stories.pB: Parents, route home and name all taken
stories.pC: She lets No-Face into the bathhouse
stories.pD: The loop of a name she is losing hold of
stories.pE: Bathhouse routine that quietly eats the years
stories.pF: She works, keeps her name, and does not look back

stories.sum: A job taken for one year on the way to something else quietly becomes the thing itself.
stories.s1: One year at Runway, described as temporary in every conversation, including the ones she has with herself.
stories.s2: Paris removes the story that she is above it. She is not visiting the arrangement, she is in it.
stories.s3: The mask is being the girl who is not really like this, worn while doing all of it.
stories.s4: She drops the phone in the fountain, mid-assignment, with nothing else arranged.
stories.pA: A year described as temporary in every conversation
stories.pB: Paris removes the story of being above it
stories.pC: She takes the Paris seat knowing what it costs Nigel
stories.pD: The loop of not really being one of them
stories.pE: The comfortable competence of doing the job well
stories.pF: She drops the phone in the fountain

stories.sum: Relentless good cheer is a real skill and also a place to stand so nothing has to be looked at.
stories.s1: Optimism as a complete operating system. It works on everyone else, which is what keeps it from being examined.
stories.s2: The divorce, the distance from his son, the panic attacks. The props come off in front of a stadium.
stories.s3: The loop is the cheer itself: kept up because stopping would leave the thing it was covering in plain view.
stories.s4: He sits down with the therapist and says the true thing, which is harder for him than any match.
stories.pA: Optimism running as a complete operating system
stories.pB: The divorce and the distance from his son
stories.pC: He hides the panic attacks and it costs him the room
stories.pD: Cheer kept up so the cover is not dropped
stories.pE: A season of routine where nothing is discussed
stories.pF: He sits down and says the true thing

stories.sum: A man goes to therapy for twenty years and uses every session to get better at not changing.
stories.s1: North Caldwell, the pool, the ducks. A suburban life run in parallel with the other one, and both described as normal.
stories.s2: The panic attacks are the collapse. His body concedes what he will not, and the props keep working while he stops.
stories.s3: Two decades of the same conversation in the same office. The insight arrives every week and never survives the drive home.
stories.s4: Refused. The show is a long study of what happens when the fourth stage is available and declined, session after session.
stories.pA: A suburban routine held alongside the other life
stories.pB: The panic attacks concede what he will not
stories.pC: Every impulsive act widens damage he then has to manage
stories.pD: The same session, the same insight, weekly, for years
stories.pE: The pool, the boat, the routine that absorbs everything
stories.pF: Absent - the exit is available and declined

stories.sum: Everyone in the city is good at their job, and the job is what keeps the city exactly as it is.
stories.s1: The stats, the clearance rate, the corner. Every institution runs a map that stopped matching the ground years ago.
stories.s2: Each season strips the props from someone: the case, the union, the school, the paper. Nobody gets to keep their cover.
stories.s3: The institutions are the cage. Individuals see clearly and are outlasted by the systems that employ them.
stories.s4: Small and local when it comes. Bunny with the free zone, Prez in the classroom, ownership taken where nobody is watching.
stories.pA: Clearance rates that describe a city nobody lives in
stories.pB: Each season takes the case, the job or the cover
stories.pC: An impatient wire, an unauthorised call, the whole detail collapses
stories.pD: The chain of command, repeating itself upward
stories.pE: The institution absorbs everything and keeps paying
stories.pF: Small local ownership, taken where nobody is watching

stories.sum: A man wears another man name for a decade and finds the disguise has no exit written into it.
stories.s1: The office, the apartment, the account. A life assembled to be looked at, and successful enough that nobody checks the seams.
stories.s2: The identity comes apart in stages: the marriage, the agency, the name. Each collapse is answered by rebuilding the same structure.
stories.s3: Don Draper is the cage, worn so long that removing it takes the whole series and most of what he owns.
stories.s4: California, the retreat, the phone call. Ownership arrives quietly and the show refuses to say what he does with it.
stories.pA: A life assembled to be looked at
stories.pB: Marriage, agency and name come apart in stages
stories.pC: Each impulsive escape costs him the ground he had gained
stories.pD: The same childhood, re-run in every hotel room
stories.pE: Another account, another apartment, another version of the same year
stories.pF: He stops in California and picks the phone up

stories.sum: Four people compete for a prize that only exists while the man offering it is alive to withhold it.
stories.s1: The plane, the compound, the birthday. Extreme comfort arranged so that no one inside it has to become an adult.
stories.s2: Each betrayal strips a position, and the props return within an episode. The collapse never quite completes, which is the trap.
stories.s3: The loop is the approval, sought from a man who withholds it on purpose. Everyone can name it and nobody can leave it.
stories.s4: Barely. The clearest act belongs to the one who takes the money and stops competing.
stories.pA: Comfort arranged so nobody has to become an adult
stories.pB: Each betrayal strips a position, briefly
stories.pC: The impulsive press conference, the leak, the vote called early
stories.pD: Approval sought from a man who withholds it
stories.pE: The jet, the compound, the endless holding pattern
stories.pF: The one who takes the money and stops competing

stories.sum: A woman tells the audience everything so that she never has to tell anyone in the room.
stories.s1: The cafe, the jokes, the same night repeated. A functioning life run on the assumption that nothing needs to be said.
stories.s2: Boo. The guilt is the collapse, and it happened before the first episode, which is why the first series is a performance.
stories.s3: The camera is the cage, made literal. She turns to us at every moment she would otherwise have to be present.
stories.s4: The last shot. She waves the audience off and stays in her own life without a witness.
stories.pA: A functioning routine where nothing has to be said
stories.pB: Boo, and the guilt underneath the whole first series
stories.pC: The impulse that cost her the friendship she is mourning
stories.pD: The turn to camera, used at every hard moment
stories.pE: The cafe and the jokes, keeping everything survivable
stories.pF: She waves us off and stays in the scene

stories.sum: A man solves grief by having the memory of it surgically switched off for eight hours a day.
stories.s1: The severed floor is the first stage built as architecture: comfort by amputation, with waffle parties as the reward structure.
stories.s2: The overtime contingency. Both selves discover the other is also trapped, and neither set of props was ever real.
stories.s3: Lumon is a predatory cage with a wellness programme. The loops are administered, scheduled and given cheerful names.
stories.s4: He wakes up outside and says a true sentence with a mouth the company does not control.
stories.pA: Comfort by amputation, with a waffle party attached
stories.pB: Both selves learn the other is trapped too
stories.pC: The escape is triggered before anyone has a plan
stories.pD: The break room, where the loop is administered
stories.pE: Perks, dance breaks and a numbered routine
stories.pF: He wakes outside and speaks with his own mouth

stories.sum: A cook inherits a debt and a grief and tries to solve both by raising the standard of the food.
stories.s1: The sandwich shop, run the way it has always been run. The routine is grief with a service to get through.
stories.s2: Michael death and the books. Everything he trained for arrives attached to a business that cannot pay its suppliers.
stories.s3: The perfectionist is the cage, inherited from the same family that produced the grief. He locks himself in a walk-in, literally.
stories.s4: Prep lists, call-backs, the same tasks in the same order, every service. Ownership here is procedural and it is daily.
stories.pA: A shop run the way it has always been run
stories.pB: The death and the books arrive together
stories.pC: The impatient opening, the unpaid invoice, the door left unlocked
stories.pD: The walk-in, and the loop he takes in there
stories.pE: Service after service, which postpones every real question
stories.pF: Prep lists and call-backs, done in order, every day

stories.sum: A man builds a second name to escape a brother judgement and then cannot get back out of it.
stories.s1: The mail room, the elder law practice, the nail salon office. Each is a legitimate life he keeps almost committing to.
stories.s2: Chuck letter, then the fire. The verdict he spent a decade arguing against turns out to have been written down.
stories.s3: Saul Goodman is the cage, and it works so well that the man who built it disappears inside it for six years.
stories.s4: The courtroom, at the end. He gives the true account under his own name and takes the sentence that follows.
stories.pA: A legitimate practice he keeps almost committing to
stories.pB: The letter, the fire, and the verdict in writing
stories.pC: Every shortcut wins the day and costs the decade
stories.pD: The brother voice, running long after the brother
stories.pE: The comfortable con, profitable and repeatable
stories.pF: He gives the true account under his own name

alt: a song of ice and fire
stories.sum: Everyone plays a game whose rules they were taught by people the game had already killed.
stories.s1: Winterfell in summer. An order so settled that honour reads as strategy and nobody has checked the assumption in a generation.
stories.s2: Ned execution and the Red Wedding. The story removes the props by removing the people who were the props.
stories.s3: The loop is the claim: each house repeats an inherited grievance and calls the repetition a right.
stories.s4: Where it works it is unglamorous - Brienne keeping an oath, Sam reading, Arya taking the ship west.
stories.pA: A settled order nobody has questioned in a generation
stories.pB: Ned execution, and every certainty after it
stories.pC: Honourable choices made too early, in the wrong room
stories.pD: An inherited grievance, repeated as a right
stories.pE: Kings Landing, where the game replaces the point of it
stories.pF: An oath kept, a book read, a ship taken west

stories.sum: Desperate people are offered a fair game, and the fairness is the most convincing lie in it.
stories.s1: The debt is normal life, and everyone in it has agreed to describe their situation as temporary bad luck.
stories.s2: The island removes name, clothes and history, and replaces them with a number. The strip is administrative and total.
stories.s3: The vote is the cage: they are allowed to leave, and they come back, which the game counts on.
stories.s4: He refuses the last move, then refuses the money for a year, then turns the plane around.
stories.pA: Debt described by everyone as temporary bad luck
stories.pB: Name, clothes and history replaced by a number
stories.pC: Alliances made in panic that cost more than they save
stories.pD: The vote, taken and reversed and taken again
stories.pE: The dormitory routine between rounds
stories.pF: He refuses the last move and turns the plane around

stories.sum: A pilot washes up somewhere the rules are entirely different and survives by learning them rather than arguing.
stories.s1: An English pilot with a mission, a crew and a certainty about his own standing. All three are era-specific and none travel.
stories.s2: The wreck takes the ship, the language, the rank and the right to speak. He is kept alive at someone else discretion.
stories.s3: The loop is his insistence on being understood on his own terms, which nearly gets him killed several times.
stories.s4: He learns the language, the customs and the tea, and stops trying to win the argument.
stories.pA: An English certainty about rank that does not travel
stories.pB: The wreck takes ship, language, rank and voice
stories.pC: Every outburst in the wrong room costs somebody their life
stories.pD: His insistence on being understood on his terms
stories.pE: Comfortable months in the village, learning nothing urgent
stories.pF: He learns the language and stops arguing

stories.sum: A man who lost a daughter is given a second one and makes a choice no one else gets to review.
stories.s1: The quarantine zone, twenty years in. A survivable routine of smuggling and rations that everybody treats as the world.
stories.s2: The first twenty minutes remove the daughter, and every subsequent loss is measured against that one.
stories.s3: The loop is the promise he made to himself never to have anything to lose again.
stories.s4: The hospital. Total ownership, executed without hesitation, in a direction he then lies about.
stories.pA: A survivable routine of rations and smuggling
stories.pB: The first loss, against which everything is measured
stories.pC: The decision at the hospital, made in minutes, unreviewed
stories.pD: The vow never to have anything to lose
stories.pE: Boston, Jackson, the safe years in between
stories.pF: He acts completely, and lies about it afterwards

stories.sum: A man with insight into exactly what is wrong with him uses the insight instead of the change.
stories.s1: The house above the hills, the residuals, the show playing on a loop. Comfort that removes any reason to be anywhere.
stories.s2: New Mexico, then the obituary, then the trial. The props are removed slowly and he replaces each one.
stories.s3: He narrates his own cage with great accuracy, which is the cage. Self-knowledge is used as a substitute for the exit.
stories.s4: Prison, and the swimming pool conversation. The ending refuses to say whether ownership held.
stories.pA: A house, residuals, and his own show on repeat
stories.pB: New Mexico, the obituary, the trial
stories.pC: Every impulsive night costs somebody else the decade
stories.pD: Accurate self-narration used instead of the exit
stories.pE: Another project, another bender, another year
stories.pF: Prison, and one conversation that is not performed

stories.sum: A rich family loses everything and discovers the loss removed the one thing keeping them apart.
stories.s1: The wealth is the bubble, and it is doing the work of a family. Nobody has needed to be known.
stories.s2: The seizure takes the house, the staff, the accounts and the wardrobe, and puts four people in two motel rooms.
stories.s3: Each of them is wearing a persona built for a room that no longer exists, and they wear it for two seasons.
stories.s4: The store, the motel purchase, the apology, the wedding. Ownership taken in small, unglamorous, repeated acts.
stories.pA: Wealth doing the work a family should have done
stories.pB: House, staff, accounts and wardrobe seized
stories.pC: Old habits spent on money that is no longer there
stories.pD: A persona kept for a room that no longer exists
stories.pE: The motel, comfortable enough to stay indefinitely
stories.pF: The store, the purchase, the apology, the wedding

stories.sum: A woman is shown every life she did not live and has to choose the one she is actually in.
stories.s1: The laundromat, the audit, the receipts. A life narrowed to admin, with the divorce papers unread on the counter.
stories.s2: The verse-jumping strips the assumption that this life is the only one, which turns out to be worse rather than better.
stories.s3: The bagel is the loop stated as an object: if everything is possible then nothing matters, on repeat.
stories.s4: She chooses the laundromat, the husband and the daughter, on purpose, with all the alternatives visible.
stories.pA: A life narrowed to receipts and an unread divorce
stories.pB: Every certainty about this life removed at once
stories.pC: She takes the fight to her daughter rather than the room
stories.pD: The bagel: if everything is possible, nothing matters
stories.pE: The audit, the taxes, the endlessly deferred conversation
stories.pF: She chooses this life with the alternatives in view

stories.sum: A family runs a clever plan beautifully and never notices the plan had no second half.
stories.s1: The semi-basement, the folded pizza boxes, the stolen wifi. Poverty run as a competent routine that nobody calls a crisis.
stories.s2: The flood. In one night the house, the belongings and the plan are gone, and the gym floor is the baseline.
stories.s3: The bunker is the cage made architectural: a man living under a house, sending messages nobody reads.
stories.s4: The son plan to buy the house is the fourth stage as fantasy - stated, costed, and out of reach.
stories.pA: Poverty run as a competent, unexamined routine
stories.pB: The flood takes the house and everything in it
stories.pC: They celebrate in the living room before the job is done
stories.pD: A man under the house, signalling to nobody
stories.pE: The comfortable weeks of being employed by the Parks
stories.pF: A plan to buy the house, costed and out of reach

stories.sum: A boy is handed a prophecy that was written for him by people who wanted him to obey it.
stories.s1: Caladan. An ordered house with an inherited role, a fencing tutor and a future everyone has already agreed on.
stories.s2: The betrayal takes the father, the house, the water and the name in a single night on an unfamiliar planet.
stories.s3: The prophecy is the cage: every step toward power confirms a story that was planted to be confirmed.
stories.s4: He learns the desert - the walk, the water discipline, the worm - and takes the role on terms he chooses.
stories.pA: An ordered house with a future already agreed
stories.pB: Father, house, water and name gone in one night
stories.pC: Every move he makes tightens the prophecy around him
stories.pD: A story planted to be confirmed by his own choices
stories.pE: The sietch years, comfortable enough to stay
stories.pF: He learns the desert and takes the role deliberately

stories.sum: A perfect day repeats until one thought arrives that the perfect day has no room for.
stories.s1: Barbieland is the first stage rendered as production design: every day identical, every problem solved before it is stated.
stories.s2: The real world removes the standing, the certainty and the flat feet. Nothing she was told about herself survives the trip.
stories.s3: The cage is the role: she is a category rather than a person, and the category cannot hold a difficult thought.
stories.s4: She chooses to be ordinary and mortal, which the film treats as the harder and less glamorous option.
stories.pA: Every day identical, every problem pre-solved
stories.pB: The real world removes the standing and the certainty
stories.pC: Ken brings back a whole ideology from one weekend
stories.pD: A category that cannot hold a difficult thought
stories.pE: The choreographed nights that keep the question away
stories.pF: She chooses to be ordinary and mortal

stories.sum: A man avoids promotion for thirty years so he never has to be responsible for anyone else.
stories.s1: Still a captain, still flying, still in the same hangar. A career arranged so that nothing can be lost twice.
stories.s2: The mission removes the option of staying peripheral. He is made responsible for the son of the man he lost.
stories.s3: The loop is Goose, running for thirty years under everything he does and every promotion he declines.
stories.s4: He teaches, then he flies the mission himself, and lets Rooster fly the half he cannot control.
stories.pA: A career arranged so nothing can be lost twice
stories.pB: The mission removes the option of staying peripheral
stories.pC: Old instincts that nearly cost the team the plan
stories.pD: Goose, running under everything for thirty years
stories.pE: The hangar, the test flights, the deferred promotion
stories.pF: He teaches, flies, and lets Rooster take the rest

stories.sum: A family holds a miracle together by never mentioning what holding it is costing each of them.
stories.s1: The casita, the gifts, the town. A functioning miracle with one rule: nobody talks about the cracks.
stories.s2: The house falls down. The gifts, the walls and the standing go together, and what is left is a family on a riverbank.
stories.s3: Each of them is locked in a role: the strong one, the perfect one, the one without a gift. Nobody can put it down.
stories.s4: They rebuild by hand, without the miracle, and the door at the end has all their names on it.
stories.pA: A functioning miracle with one unspoken rule
stories.pB: The house falls and takes the gifts with it
stories.pC: Mirabel forces it open before anyone is ready
stories.pD: A role nobody in the family can put down
stories.pE: The town celebration that keeps the cracks unmentioned
stories.pF: They rebuild the house by hand, without the gift

stories.sum: A woman learns a language that shows her the whole of a life, including the part that ends.
stories.s1: The lecture hall, the empty house, the routine of a grief that is being read as an ordinary quiet life.
stories.s2: The ships remove every assumption about time, language and what knowing something in advance is worth.
stories.s3: The loop is the military instinct in the room: twelve nations, all repeating a defensive reading of the same word.
stories.s4: She makes the call herself, and then chooses the life knowing exactly what it costs.
stories.pA: A quiet routine standing in for an unexamined grief
stories.pB: The ships remove every assumption about time
stories.pC: Twelve nations reading one word as a threat
stories.pD: A defensive reading, repeated in every capital
stories.pE: Protocol, briefings, and the comfort of procedure
stories.pF: She makes the call and chooses the life anyway

stories.sum: They escape across a desert to a green place, and the green place has been gone for years.
stories.s1: The Citadel runs on manufactured scarcity and a religion built to explain it. Dependence is engineered and called order.
stories.s2: The run strips the rig, the fuel, the crew and finally the destination. The green place is salt and nothing.
stories.s3: The cage is the flight itself: motion mistaken for direction, with the whole plan pointed at a memory.
stories.s4: They turn the rig around and take the place they fled, which is the harder half of the film.
stories.pA: Manufactured scarcity, delivered as religion
stories.pB: The rig, the fuel, the crew and the destination gone
stories.pC: Years spent driving toward a place that no longer exists
stories.pD: Motion mistaken for direction
stories.pE: The bikers years in the salt, waiting it out
stories.pF: They turn around and take the Citadel

stories.sum: A house is haunted by an act that was a mother only available choice, and the past will not stay past.
stories.s1: 124 and its quiet. A life arranged around not remembering, held together by keeping the doors and the conversation shut.
stories.s2: Freedom removes nothing that was taken. The collapse is behind her and the book refuses to let it stay there.
stories.s3: Beloved is the loop given a body: the past arrives, moves in, and eats everything offered to it.
stories.s4: The women at the gate, and Paul D at the end saying they need some kind of tomorrow.
stories.pA: A house arranged around not remembering
stories.pB: Freedom that returns nothing already taken
stories.pC: A choice made in minutes that governs thirty years
stories.pD: The past arrives, moves in, and is fed
stories.pE: The quiet of 124, with the doors kept shut
stories.pF: The women at the gate, and a tomorrow named

stories.sum: A woman takes three marriages to find out that the pear tree was a standard, not a daydream.
stories.s1: The porch, the store, the position as the mayor wife. Comfort and standing arranged by someone else, on her behalf.
stories.s2: Eatonville ends, then the hurricane and the water take the rest. She comes back with nothing but the telling of it.
stories.s3: The cage is the head-rag and the counter: a role assigned to her, defended by a husband who calls it protection.
stories.s4: She leaves with Tea Cake, works the muck, and comes home to tell the story in her own voice.
stories.pA: Standing arranged for her by somebody else
stories.pB: The hurricane and the water take the rest
stories.pC: The dog, the bite, the choice that follows
stories.pD: A role defended by a husband as protection
stories.pE: Twenty years behind the store counter
stories.pF: She works the muck and tells it in her own voice

stories.sum: A boy stays silent in an alley for one minute and spends the next twenty-six years paying for it.
stories.s1: Kabul before the war: the house, the kites, the servant who is also the friend. An order nobody in it examines.
stories.s2: The invasion takes the country, the house and the standing. California is a petrol station and a flea market stall.
stories.s3: The alley runs on a loop for twenty-six years, and the successful life in America is built directly on top of it.
stories.s4: He goes back, takes the beating, and brings the boy home. Ownership is literal and it costs him.
stories.pA: A household order nobody in it examines
stories.pB: The invasion takes the country and the house
stories.pC: One minute of silence in an alley
stories.pD: The same minute, replayed for twenty-six years
stories.pE: A comfortable American life built over it
stories.pF: He goes back, takes the beating, brings the boy home

stories.sum: A man builds everything in opposition to his father and cannot bend when the ground itself moves.
stories.s1: Umuofia, and a standing earned by work. The order is real, functioning, and assumed to be permanent by everyone in it.
stories.s2: Exile, then the mission, then the district commissioner. The world he mastered is replaced while he is away from it.
stories.s3: The cage is the fear of being his father, which decides every choice he makes including the ones that ruin him.
stories.s4: Refused. He acts decisively at the end, and the book is clear that decisiveness is not the same as ownership.
stories.pA: A functioning order assumed to be permanent
stories.pB: Exile, and a world replaced while he is away
stories.pC: The killing of Ikemefuna, done to look strong
stories.pD: The fear of being his father, deciding everything
stories.pE: Seven years in his mother village, waiting to return
stories.pF: He acts decisively, which is not the same as ownership

stories.sum: Seven generations repeat the same names and the same mistakes, and the book lets them.
stories.s1: Macondo before the road: a town so complete in itself that the outside world arrives as a rumour and a novelty.
stories.s2: The banana company, the massacre, the rain. Everything the town believed about itself is removed in stages.
stories.s3: The names are the loop, printed on the page: Aureliano after Aureliano, each one repeating what the last one learned.
stories.s4: Refused, deliberately. The manuscript is read at the moment the wind takes the town, and nobody gets to act on it.
stories.pA: A town complete in itself, with no outside
stories.pB: The company, the massacre and the rain
stories.pC: Each generation makes the same choice slightly earlier
stories.pD: The same names, repeating down the family
stories.pE: Years of rain, and the house closing in on itself
stories.pF: Absent - the reading arrives with the wind

stories.sum: Four sisters are offered one acceptable future each, and one of them keeps writing anyway.
stories.s1: The attic, the plays, the four of them. A world that ends at the garden wall and is entirely sufficient inside it.
stories.s2: Beth, and the marriages, and the war. The version where they stay as they are is removed one person at a time.
stories.s3: Jo cage is the refusal to be softened, held so firmly that it costs her Laurie and nearly costs her the writing.
stories.s4: The manuscript, written nightly at speed in a cap, and sold on terms she partly loses and partly sets.
stories.pA: A world that ends at the garden wall
stories.pB: Beth, the marriages, the war
stories.pC: She burns the manuscript, and refuses Laurie in the same year
stories.pD: A refusal to be softened, held past its use
stories.pE: The comfortable years of keeping the four of them intact
stories.pF: The manuscript, written nightly and sold

stories.sum: A man does the hardest work of his life and then leaves the room rather than answer for it.
stories.s1: Ingolstadt, the study, the certainty. A young man inside his own project, with the world reduced to the next result.
stories.s2: The creature opens its eyes and every assumption goes: the science, the standing, the family, one member at a time.
stories.s3: The loop is the secret. He knows the whole answer and repeats the decision not to say it, in every chapter.
stories.s4: Barely, and too late. The pursuit north is ownership arriving after everything it might have saved.
stories.pA: A young man alone inside his own project
stories.pB: The creature opens its eyes and everything goes
stories.pC: He walks out of the room the moment it works
stories.pD: The secret, kept and re-kept in every chapter
stories.pE: Convalescence, travel, and long delays before speaking
stories.pF: The pursuit north, taken far too late

stories.sum: A man is buried alive by three signatures and comes back with the patience they never accounted for.
stories.s1: The promotion, the engagement, the ship. A future so settled that a letter written in an afternoon can take all of it.
stories.s2: The Chateau d If. Fourteen years, the name, the fiancee, the father. There is nothing left to remove.
stories.s3: The Count is the cage he built to escape the cell, and by the end he cannot tell which parts of him it holds.
stories.s4: He stops the machine he built, gives the fortune away, and lets the last two of them live.
stories.pA: A future so settled a single letter can take it
stories.pB: Fourteen years, the name, the father, the engagement
stories.pC: One denunciation written in an afternoon
stories.pD: The plan, refined nightly for fourteen years
stories.pE: The Count comfortable life, which delays the reckoning
stories.pF: He stops the machine and gives the fortune away
